subject.title: Externally-registered cron jobs auto-enable without user confirmation, inherit expensive default model, no usage circuit breaker

question: What default security policy should OpenClaw apply to externally or plugin-registered recurring agentTurn cron jobs before they can run on inherited provider/model defaults?
rationale: The source reproduction is clear, but the fix changes shipped cron defaults, plugin scheduling contracts, provider/model cost policy, quota thresholds, and upgrade behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the boundary.

options.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
options.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring externally/plugin-registered agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

options.title: Narrow inherited-model guard
options.body: Keep current activation semantics but warn or block when a recurring agentTurn job inherits an expensive default model without an explicit job model.

options.title: Split to canonical subissues
options.body: Resolve provenance, cost budgets, and reason-aware circuit breakers through the related open issues while leaving this issue as the cluster index until all parts land.

recommendation.title: Coordinated cron safety policy
recommendation.body: Require operator-visible activation or approval for recurring externally/plugin-registered agentTurn jobs, add model-cost visibility, and pair any breaking default change with doctor/update migration guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has history on the plugin scheduled-turn/runtime seam and appears in related cron guardrail review context, making this the best available product/security routing candidate.
